observation.visible_scene: A workshop/garage against a cinder-block wall: a large flat circular disc (pale tan, like cardboard/thin wood) is mounted vertically on a wooden post on a workbench. A straight wooden bar (arm) is fixed through the disc's center (a yellow hub with a dark bolt), with a blue T-handle/clamp on one end and metal nuts/weights on the other. Background props (step ladder, hanging broom, blue pry bar, open toolbox on a shelf, scattered tools) remain in fixed positions throughout.
visible_changes: The wooden arm assembly rotates continuously about the central yellow hub, sweeping through a full circle repeatedly; the blue handle and the opposite bar tip move in a steady clockwise arc in the image plane (e.g., handle goes from ~4-5 o'clock to ~6, ~9, ~12, ~3 and back).
The blue handle and the metal weights show motion blur, indicating the arm is spinning at a constant, fairly fast rate; the blur is strongest when the handle is near the horizontal positions.
The arm stays a straight bar through the hub, with the handle and the far tip remaining diametrically opposite as it turns.
The background and the disc's outline do not change position, so the apparent motion is object rotation, not camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What started the rotation (hand spin, motor, etc.) and whether the spin continues, slows, or stops after the last frame.
Whether the disc itself is rotating about its axis (its surface is too uniform to confirm from these frames).
The true 3D orientation / whether the rotation axis is exactly perpendicular to the camera.
uncertain_details: Exact angular speed and period (roughly one revolution per ~15 sampled frames, but not precisely measurable).
Whether the camera is perfectly fixed or has negligible drift (background cues suggest fixed).
Material identities of the disc, bar, handle, and weights (only appearance is visible).
